paragraphs: American Coastal Insurance Corporation (referred to in this Form 10-K as we, our, us, the Company or ACIC) is a holding company primarily engaged in the commercial property and casualty insurance business with investments in the United States. On July 10, 2023, we changed our corporate name from United Insurance Holdings Corp. to American Coastal Insurance Corporation. We conduct our business principally through our wholly owned insurance subsidiary, American Coastal Insurance Company (AmCoastal). The Company also previously wrote insurance outside of Florida through Interboro Insurance Company (IIC); however, on April 1, 2025, the Company completed the sale of IIC. The details of this transaction are described below. Collectively, we refer to the holding company and all our subsidiaries, including non-insurance subsidiaries, as "American Coastal Insurance Corporation," which is the preferred brand identification for our Company.

Our Company's revenue is generated from writing insurance in Florida. Our target market in such areas consists of states where the perceived threat of natural catastrophe has caused large national insurance carriers to reduce their concentration of policies. We believe an opportunity exists for ACIC to write profitable business in such areas. In 2023, our former insurance subsidiary that wrote personal residential business in six states, United Property & Casualty Insurance Company (UPC) was placed into receivership with the Florida Department of Financial Services (the "DFS"), which divested our ownership of UPC. The results of this subsidiary for periods prior to receivership, now included within discontinued operations, can be seen in Note 4 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements below. Discussion of 2023 and 2024 related to UPC can be found in our 2023 and 2024 Forms 10-K.

We have historically grown our business through strong organic growth, complemented by strategic acquisitions and partnerships, including our acquisitions of AmCo Holding Company, LLC (AmCo) and its subsidiaries, including AmCoastal, in April 2017.

On May 9, 2024, we entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Sale Agreement") with Forza Insurance Holdings, LLC (Forza) in which ACIC agreed to sell and Forza agreed to acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding stock of IIC. Forza's application to acquire IIC was approved by the New York Department of Financial Services ("NYDFS") on February 13, 2025, and the sale closed on April 1, 2025. The Company received cash proceeds totaling $25,679,000 from the sale resulting in a loss on disposal of $247,000, net of tax impacts. The Company also recognized a $1,348,000 loss, net of tax impacts, on IIC's fixed maturity portfolio, which was included in accumulated other comprehensive loss on the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheets prior to the sale. As a result, IIC results of operations and assets and liabilities are captured within discontinued operations and can be seen in Note 4 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements below.

Financial strength or stability ratings are important to insurance companies in establishing their competitive position and may impact an insurance company's ability to write policies. We are rated by Demotech and Kroll Bond Rating Agency (Kroll). Demotech maintains a letter-scale financial stability rating system ranging from A'' (A double prime) to L (licensed by insurance regulatory authorities). Kroll maintains a letter-scale financial strength rating system for insurance companies ranging from AAA (extremely strong operations and no risk) to R (operating under regulatory supervision). The financial strength or stability ratings of our insurance company subsidiary as of December 31, 2025 are listed below. With these ratings, we expect our property insurance policies will be acceptable to the secondary mortgage marketplace and mortgage lenders.

Our vision is to be a top-quartile underwriter of catastrophe-exposed property insurance. Our plan is to focus primarily on low-rise commercial property insurance in Florida. We write our condominium product through our exclusive managing general agency agreement and long-term partnership with AmRisc. In addition, in 2025 we began writing our apartment and assisted living products through our affiliated managing general agency Skyway Underwriters. The Company's continuous portfolio optimization process strives to balance our risk appetite and underwriting profit opportunities with our available capital and reinsurance capacity to achieve consistent and sustainable underwriting profitability for the Company and its reinsurers over time.

We desire to have the right combination of price, underwriting rules, deductibles and coverages to earn a return on capital that exceeds our cost of capital throughout the insurance market cycle. The Company also seeks to have risks maintain an appropriate insurance to value through re-underwriting and inspections of each property every three years to ensure it meets or exceeds our underwriting guidelines with verified data quality and integrity regarding the key risk characteristics of our covered properties.

We provide commercial multi-peril property insurance for residential condominium associations, apartments and assisted living facilities in Florida. We include coverage to policyholders for loss or damage to buildings, inventory or equipment caused by covered causes of loss such as fire, wind, hail, water, theft and vandalism.
On our equipment breakdown, identity theft, and flood policies we earn a commission while retaining no risk of loss, since all such risk is ceded to other private companies (other risks).

We price our products at levels that we project will generate an acceptable underwriting profit. We aim to accurately underwrite the risk and profitability of each potential policy. The Company uses pricing algorithms, judgment-based rating and consent to rate methodologies that consider historical attritional loss costs for the rating territory in which the risk resides, as well as modeled expected losses for catastrophes and projected reinsurance costs based on the specific geographic and structural characteristics of the property. We seek to optimize our portfolio by managing our probable maximum loss (PML), total insured value (TIV) and average annual loss (AAL). As a part of this optimization process, we use the output from third-party modeling software to analyze our risk exposures, including wind exposures, by zip code or street address. We also utilize AI technology to assist with the intake process and the underwriting evaluation process (including both guidelines and building characteristics).

We measure our underwriting profitability by the combined ratio, which is a sum of the ratios of losses, loss adjustment expenses, and underwriting expenses to either gross or net earned premiums. A combined ratio under 100% indicates an underwriting profit. Refer to Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in Part II, Item 7 of this report for further details on our combined ratio.

Our condominium policies are marketed and distributed by AmRisc through a network of independent agencies managed by AmRisc that specialize in commercial residential insurance. AmRisc is an unaffiliated third party and represents 100% of our condominium revenue based on our exclusive agreement in Florida.

Our apartment and assisted living facility policies are marketed and distributed by Skyway Underwriters through multiple wholesaler partners that specialize in commercial residential insurance. These wholesalers represented 100% of our apartment and assisted living facility revenue.

The Company believes wholesale partners build relationships in their communities that can lead to profitable business and policyholder satisfaction. We believe we have built significant credibility and loyalty with the wholesale communities in Florida through (i) our frequent in-depth communications on our products and (ii) our expectations and goals for our relationships with each wholesaler.

headings: Because we rely on insurance agents, the loss of these agent relationships, particularly our relationship with AmRisc, or our inability to attract and incentivize new agents could have an adverse impact on our business.
Actual claims incurred may exceed our loss reserves for claims, which could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
We face risks associated with investments in which we share ownership or management with third parties.
Because we are operating in a highly competitive market, we may lack the resources to control our market share, which could adversely impact our business and results of operations.
Changes in state regulation may adversely affect our results of operation and financial condition.
The insurance industry is heavily regulated and further restrictive regulation may reduce our profitability and limit our growth.

Our inability to obtain reinsurance on acceptable terms could increase our loss exposure or limit our ability to underwrite policies, which could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Our inability to collect from our reinsurers on our reinsurance claims could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operation, financial condition and cash flow.
We may fail to pay claims accurately and timely, which could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Our investments are subject to market risks that may result in reduced returns or losses.
The property and casualty insurance and reinsurance industries are historically cyclical and the pricing and terms for our products may decline, which would adversely affect our profitability.
Losses from legal actions may materially affect our operating results, cash flows and financial condition.
A downgrade in or withdrawal of our financial strength or stability ratings could adversely impact our business volume and our ability to access additional debt or equity financing.
Future sales of substantial amounts of our common stock by us or our existing stockholders could cause our stock price to decrease.
Dividend payments on our common stock in the future are uncertain, and our ability to pay dividends may be constrained by our holding company structure.
The ability of our insurance subsidiary to pay dividends may affect our liquidity and ability to meet our obligations.
paragraphs: Many factors affect our business, financial condition and results of operations, some of which are beyond our control. If any of the following risks or uncertainties occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations may be materially and adversely affected. In that event, the trading price of our securities could decline, and investors could lose all or part of their investment in our securities. Before making an investment in our securities, investors should carefully consider the risk factors discussed below, together with the other information in this report, including the section entitled "Forward-looking Statements" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and the other reports and materials filed by us with the SEC.

As a property and casualty insurer, we may experience significant losses, and our financial results may vary from period to period, due to our exposure to catastrophic events and severe weather conditions, the frequency and severity of which could be affected by the unpredictability of future catastrophic events and severe weather conditions.

Our property and casualty insurance operations expose us to risks arising from catastrophes. Catastrophes can be caused by various natural events, including but not limited to hurricanes, tropical storms, tornadoes, windstorms, earthquakes, hail, sinkholes, severe winter weather and fires, or man-made events, such as terrorist attacks (including those involving nuclear, biological, chemical or radiological events), cybercrimes or consequences of war or political instability. paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. The following discussion provides an analysis of our results of operations and financial condition for 2025 as compared to 2024. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain known and unknown risks and uncertainties. See "Forward-Looking Statements."

During the periods presented, we conducted our business principally through our wholly owned insurance subsidiary, American Coastal Insurance Company (AmCoastal). Collectively, we refer to the holding company and all our subsidiaries, including non-insurance subsidiaries, as "ACIC," which is the preferred brand identification for our Company.

On February 27, 2023, our former insurance subsidiary that wrote personal residential business in six states, United Property & Casualty Insurance Company (UPC) was placed into receivership with the Florida Department of Financial Services (the "DFS"), which divested our ownership of UPC. The events leading to receivership and results of this subsidiary, now included within discontinued operations, can be seen in Note 4 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements below.

On May 9, 2024, we entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Sale Agreement") with Forza Insurance Holdings, LLC (Forza) in which ACIC agreed to sell and Forza agreed to acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding stock of IIC. Forza's application to acquire IIC was approved by the New York Department of Financial Services ("NYDFS") on February 13, 2025, and the sale closed on April 1, 2025. As a result, IIC results of operations and assets and liabilities are captured within discontinued operations and can be seen in Note 4 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements below.

We have historically grown our business through strong organic growth, complemented by strategic acquisitions and partnerships, including our acquisitions of AmCo Holding Company, LLC (AmCo) and its subsidiaries, including AmCoastal, in April 2017.
Our policies in-force increased by 5.20% from 4,099 policies in-force at December 31, 2024, to 4,311 policies in-force at December 31, 2025.

Our business is subject to the impact of weather-related catastrophes on our loss and loss adjustment expenses (LAE). During the year ended December 31, 2025, no named storms made landfall in our geographic footprint. During the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, five and two named storms, respectively, made landfall in our geographic footprint, resulting in retained pre-tax catastrophe losses of $25,442,000 and $729,000 respectively.

For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we have consolidated our Operating and Underwriting Expenses and General and Administrative Expenses lines within our Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income into the General and Administrative Expenses line. This was done in an effort to align more closely with our peer group for comparability. Accordingly, we have recast our Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income for the year ended December 31, 2023 to align with this format. We have also added a new note to our consolidated financial statements, Note 3, Disaggregation of Relevant Expense Captions, to provide the users of our financial statements with enhanced insight into this expense line.

The following discussion highlights significant factors influencing the consolidated financial position and results of operations of ACIC. In evaluating our results of operations, we use premiums written and earned, policies in-force and new and renewal policies by geographic concentration. We also consider the impact of catastrophe losses and prior year development on our loss ratios, expense ratios and combined ratios. In monitoring our investments, we use credit quality, investment income, cash flows, realized gains and losses, unrealized gains and losses, asset diversification and portfolio duration. To evaluate our financial condition, we consider our liquidity, financial strength, ratings, book value per share and return on equity.

paragraphs: American Coastal Insurance Corporation (以下稱為本公司，或 ACIC) 為一間主要從事商業不動產及意外險業務的控股公司，並在美國進行投資。於 2023 年 7 月 10 日，本公司將公司名稱由 United Insurance Holdings Corp. 改為 American Coastal Insurance Corporation。本公司主要透過本公司全資擁有之保險子公司 American Coastal Insurance Company (AmCoastal) 進行業務。本公司也曾經透過 Interboro Insurance Company (IIC) 在佛羅裏達州以外地區寫單，但於 2025 年 4 月 1 日，本公司完成 IIC 的出售。此交易之細節於下文說明。總體而言，本公司稱控股公司及所有子公司，包括非保險子公司，為 "American Coastal Insurance Corporation"，為本公司之首選品牌識別。

本公司之營業收入來自於佛羅裏達州寫單。本公司在這些地區之目標市場為那些因自然災害之威脅被認為較高，導致大型國家保險電信業者減少其保單集中度之州。本公司認為 ACIC 在這些地區有機會寫出獲利之業務。2023 年，本公司曾寫個人住宅業務之前保險子公司 United Property & Casualty Insurance Company (UPC)，於佛羅裏達州財政服務部 ("DFS") 被置於監督狀態，並讓本公司放棄對 UPC 之擁有權。此子公司在被置於監督狀態前之營運結果，現已納入已終止營運項目，可見於下文財務報表附註第 4 項。有關 2023 年及 2024 年與 UPC 有關之說明，可見於本公司 2023 年及 2024 年之 Form 10-K。
本公司歷來透過強勁之內生成長，配合戰略性收購與合作夥伴關係，包括於 2017 年 4 月收購 AmCo Holding Company, LLC (AmCo) 及其子公司，包括 AmCoastal，來擴張業務。

於 2024 年 5 月 9 日，本公司與 Forza Insurance Holdings, LLC (Forza) 簽訂股票買賣協議 ("Sale Agreement")，ACIC 同意出售，Forza 同意收購 IIC 100% 發行在外之股票。Forza 申請收購 IIC 獲得紐約財政服務部 ("NYDFS") 批准為 2025 年 2 月 13 日，並於 2025 年 4 月 1 日完成交易。本公司從此交易中收到現金總計 25,679,000 美元，導致處置損失 247,000 美元，扣除稅務影響。本公司亦認列 IIC 固定成熟投資組合之損失 1,348,000 美元，扣除稅務影響，此損失已包含於本公司財務報表合併資產負債表之累積其他綜合損益中，於出售前。因此，IIC 之營運結果及資產與負債已納入已終止營運項目，可見於下文財務報表附註第 4 項。

財務強度或穩定性評級對保險公司建立其競爭地位至關重要，並可能影響保險公司寫單之能力。本公司由 Demotech 及 Kroll Bond Rating Agency (Kroll) 進行評級。Demotech 保有字母評級之財務穩定性評級系統，從 A'' (A 雙引號) 到 L (經保險監管機關許可)。Kroll 保有字母評級之財務強度評級系統，適用於保險公司，從 AAA (極強之營運，無風險) 到 R (於監管監督下營運)。本公司保險子公司截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之財務強度或穩定性評級如下。憑藉這些評級，本公司預期其不動產保險保單將被次級房貸市場及房貸貸款人接受。

本公司願景為成為暴露於災害之不動產保險之前四分之一之承保人。本公司計畫主要專注於佛羅裏達州之低層商業不動產保險。本公司透過與 AmRisc 之獨家管理總代理協議及長期合作夥伴關係，寫出其公寓產品。此外，於 2025 年本公司開始透過本公司關聯之管理總代理 Skyway Underwriters，寫出其公寓及輔助生活產品。本公司持續之投資組合最佳化流程，致力於平衡本公司之風險承受能力與承保獲利機會，與本公司之可用資本及再保險容量，以實現本公司及其再保險人之持續且可持續之承保獲利。
本公司希望擁有適當之價格、承保規則、免賠額與保障，以在保險市場週期中獲取超過本公司資本成本之回報。本公司亦希望風險維持適當之保險價值，透過重新評估及每三年對每一不動產進行檢查，以確保其符合或超越本公司之承保指引，並有驗證之資料品質與誠信，以確保本公司所覆蓋不動產之關鍵風險特徵。
本公司為佛羅裏達州之住宅公寓協會、公寓及輔助生活設施提供商業多風險不動產保險。本公司為保單持有人提供因覆蓋原因之損失或損害，包括火災、風暴、冰雹、水、竊盜及破壞，對建築物、存貨或設備之保障。
在本公司設備損壞、身分盜竊及水災保險政策上，我們賺取佣金，同時不承擔任何損失風險，因為所有風險均已轉移給其他私人公司（其他風險）。

我們以預期可產生可接受承保獲利的價格銷售產品。我們致力於準確評估每項潛在保單的風險與獲利性。本公司使用定價演算法、基於判斷的評分及同意評分方法，考量歷史損失成本，以評估風險所在地區的損失成本，以及針對災難的模型預期損失及根據特定地理與結構特徵的財產所預測的再保險成本。我們透過管理我們的預期最大損失（PML）、總保額（TIV）及年均損失（AAL）來優化我們的投資組合。作為此優化過程的一部分，我們使用第三方建模軟體的輸出，以分析我們的風險敞口，包括風災風險，按郵遞區號或街道地址進行分析。我們也利用人工智能技術協助入會流程及承保評估流程（包括指導方針及建築特徵）。
我們以綜合比率來衡量承保獲利性，該比率為損失、損失調整費用及承保費用與總計或淨收取 premiums 的比率總和。綜合比率低於 100% 表示承保獲利。有關我們綜合比率的更多細節，請參閱本報告第二部分第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」。
我們的公寓大廈保險政策由 AmRisc 透過一個由 AmRisc 管理的獨立代理網路進行行銷與分銷，這些代理專門從事商業住宅保險。AmRisc 是一個無關聯的第三方，根據我們在佛羅裏達州的獨家協議，代表本公司 100% 的公寓大廈收入。
我們的公寓及輔助生活設施保險政策由 Skyway Underwriters 透過多個經銷商夥伴進行行銷與分銷，這些經銷商專門從事商業住宅保險。這些經銷商代表我們公寓及輔助生活設施收入的 100%。
本公司認為經銷商夥伴在其社區中建立關係，可以帶來獲利的業務與保單持有人滿意度。我們認為透過（i）我們頻繁深入的產品溝通，以及（ii）我們對每個經銷商關係的期望與目標，我們已在佛羅裏達州的經銷商社區中建立了顯著的聲譽與忠誠度。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本Form 10-K第二部分，第8項所載之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。以下討論提供對2025年營運成果及財務狀況的分析，與2024年比較。2024年營運成果及財務狀況與2023年比較的討論，請參閱我們2024年12月31日財年所屬之Form 10-K年度報告第二部分，第7項。本討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性與假設。實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所表達或暗示者有重大差異，係因某些已知與未知的風險與不確定性所致。請參閱「前瞻性陳述」。

American Coastal Insurance Corporation為一主要從事商業財產與意外保險業務之控股公司，並於美國進行投資。2023年7月10日，我們將公司名稱由United Insurance Holdings Corp.更名為American Coastal Insurance Corporation。在本報告期間內，我們主要透過我們全資擁有之保險子公司American Coastal Insurance Company (AmCoastal)進行業務。我們 collectively 會稱該控股公司與所有子公司，包括非保險子公司，為「ACIC」，這是我們公司之首選品牌識別。

本公司之營業收入來自於佛羅裏達州之保險業務。我們在這些地區之目標市場為那些因自然災害威脅被認為較高，導致大型國家保險電信業者減少其政策集中度之州。我們認為ACIC在這些地區有機會寫入獲利業務。2023年2月27日，我們前一間寫入六州個人住宅業務之保險子公司United Property & Casualty Insurance Company (UPC)，被佛羅裏達州財政服務部（「DFS」）納入清算，導致我們放棄對UPC之所有權。導致清算之事件與該子公司之結果，現已納入已終止營運，請參閱下列財務報表附註第4項。

2024年5月9日，我們與Forza Insurance Holdings, LLC (Forza)簽訂股票買賣協議（「買賣協議」），ACIC同意出售，Forza同意收購IIC全部已發行且在流通之股權。Forza取得IIC之申請於2025年2月13日獲紐約財政服務部（「NYDFS」）批准，買賣於2025年4月1日完成。本公司從買賣中收到現金總計25,679,000美元，導致處置損失247,000美元，扣除稅務影響。本公司亦認列IIC固定成熟投資組合之損失1,348,000美元，扣除稅務影響，此損失已包含於本公司合併財務報表之累積其他綜合損益中，於買賣前。因此，IIC之營運成果與資產與負債已納入已終止營運，請參閱下列財務報表附註第4項。
我們過去主要透過強勁的內生成長，配合戰略性收購與合作夥伴關係，包括2017年4月收購AmCo Holding Company, LLC (AmCo)及其子公司，包括AmCoastal，來擴張業務。
我們之保單數目由2024年12月31日之4,099張保單增加至2025年12月31日之4,311張保單，成長5.20%。
我們之業務受天氣相關災難對我們之損失與損失調整費用（LAE）之影響。2025年12月31日財年，無已命名風暴在我們之地理範圍內登陸。2024年12月31日財年與2023年12月31日財年，分別有五與兩個已命名風暴在我們之地理範圍內登陸，導致保留稅前災難損失分別為25,442,000美元與729,000美元。
2025年12月31日財年與2024年12月31日財年，我們已將營運與理賠費用與一般及行政費用線納入合併綜合損益表中的一般及行政費用線。此舉為使我們更接近同業羣組，以提高可比性。因此，我們已重新整理2023年12月31日財年之合併綜合損益表，以符合此格式。我們亦已新增一項財務報表附註，附註3，相關費用項目 disaggregation，以提供財務報表使用者對此費用線更深入的洞察。

以下討論說明影響 ACIC 合併財務狀況及營運結果的重要因素。在評估我們營運結果時，我們使用已寫單與已賺單、在劵數量及新保與續保保單按地理集中度分類。我們也會考量災害損失及前一年度損失發展對我們損失率、費用率及綜合損失率的影響。在監測我們的投資時，我們使用信用品質、投資收入、現金流、已實現損益、未實現損益、資產分散化及投資組合期限。在評估我們財務狀況時，我們考量我們的流動性、財務強度、評級、每股帳面價值及權益回報率。

headings: 因為我們依賴保險經紀人，失去這些經紀人關係，特別是與 AmRisc 的關係，或我們無法吸引並激勵新經紀人，可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
實際發生的索賠金額可能高於我們為索賠所做的備抵賠款，這可能會對我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們面臨與第三方共同擁有或管理投資相關的風險。
因為我們處於一個高度競爭的市場，我們可能缺乏資源來控制市場佔有率，這可能會對我們的業務與營運結果產生不利影響。
州政府規範的變動可能會對我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
保險業受到嚴格監管，進一步的限制性規範可能會降低我們的獲利能力並限制我們的成長。
我們無法在可接受的條件下取得再保險，可能會增加我們的損失風險或限制我們承保保單的能力，這可能會對我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們無法從再保險人處收回再保險索賠金額，可能會對我們的業務、營運結果、財務狀況與現金流產生重大不利影響。
我們可能無法準確且及時支付聲請，這可能會對我們的營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們的投資面臨市場風險，可能會導致回報減少或產生損失。
財產及意外保險與再保險產業歷來具有週期性，我們產品的價格與條款可能下降，這將對我們的獲利能力造成不利影響。
法律訴訟造成的損失可能對我們的營運成果、現金流及財務狀況產生重大影響。
我們的財務強度或穩定性評級遭降級或撤回，可能會對我們的業務規模及取得額外債務或權益融資的能力造成不利影響。
未來若我們或現有股東出售大量普通股，可能會導致我們的股票價格下跌。
未來對普通股支付股息的金額不確定，我們支付股息的能力可能受到控股公司架構的限制。
我們的保險子公司支付股息的能力可能影響我們的流動性及履行義務的能力。
paragraphs: 許多因素會影響我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果，其中一些因素超出我們的控制範圍。若下列風險或不確定性中的任何一項發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，我們的證券交易價格可能下跌，投資人可能損失全部或部分投資於我們證券的金額。在做出投資我們證券的決定前，投資人應仔細考慮下列所討論的風險因素，並配合本報告中的其他資訊，包括「預測性陳述」及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」等節，以及我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的其他報告與資料。
作為一家財產與責任保險公司，我們可能面臨重大損失，且財務結果可能因期與期之間的差異而有所變動，這是因為我們對災難事件與嚴峻天氣條件的暴露所致，而這些事件與天氣條件的發生頻率與嚴重程度可能受到未來災難事件與嚴峻天氣條件不可預測性影響。
我們的財產與責任保險業務會使我們面臨因災難事件而產生的風險。災難事件可能由多種自然現象造成，包括但不限於颶風、熱帶氣旋、龍捲風、風暴、地震、冰雹、地面塌陷、嚴峻冬季天氣及火災，或人為事件，例如恐怖攻擊（包括涉及核能、生物、化學或放射性事件的攻擊）、網路犯罪或戰爭或政治不穩定的後果。我們可能產生的災難損失金額可能超過：
• 過去年份所經歷的災難損失金額；
• 使用第三方災難模型軟體預估將產生的災難損失金額；或
• 用以開發我們產品價格的災難損失估計值
